column3: Our current architecture is modular and well-structured for future scaling.

column5: What’s your view on the current platform’s ability to scale with business growth?
column6: Where do you see the biggest architectural risks to delivering on our long-term strategy?
column7: How confident are you that we can decouple key business capabilities from the existing monolith?
column8: What’s your appetite for investing in foundational platform work versus feature delivery?
column9: Are there areas where you feel we’re “stuck” in the current stack, and what’s holding us back?
column10: The org supports skill development time.
column11: How well do you think our current delivery structure supports agility and accountability?

column13: Where do you see the biggest gaps in capability, and how are we addressing them?
column14: How empowered do teams feel to make architectural or technical decisions?
column15: Are there systemic factors (e.g. incentive structures, reporting lines) that limit team autonomy or effectiveness?
column16: Business leaders are aware of key technical bottlenecks that limit growth or innovation.
column17: Governance policies are flexible and enable delivery.
column18: Decision-making is decentralised when it makes sense.
column19: Technical changes can be traced to business goals.
column20: There’s an active feedback loop between tech and governance.
column21: Cross-functional initiatives don’t stall due to unclear ownership.
column22: Risk is identified and mitigated early in delivery.
column23: Compliance and audit needs are not a blocker.
column24: Are our governance structures supporting or slowing down delivery?
column25: How well do you think we balance innovation and risk management?
column26: Do teams have the right guardrails (not handcuffs) to deliver independently?
column27: How visible and actionable are technical delivery metrics at the leadership level?
column28: Where do you see the biggest risks in delivery or service ownership — and how are they currently managed?
column29: We have a shared understanding across departments of what success looks like for this migration.
column30: Data silos are actively being addressed.
column31: How well do you think we manage integration complexity as the business grows?
column32: Are there clear lines of accountability when integration issues affect business operations?
column33: How mature is our organisation’s thinking around data ownership and stewardship?
column34: Where do you see the biggest gaps in observability or trust in our data pipelines?
column35: Are our current systems ready to scale in terms of integration volume and velocity?

column37: There is a strong executive sponsor for platform modernisation.
column38: Product and tech share a roadmap and vision.
column39: Funding exists for foundational infrastructure work.
column40: The business is willing to defer features for platform readiness.
column41: Teams have the autonomy to pursue strategic tech work.
column42: There is a realistic expectation for migration timelines.
column44: Stakeholders are aware of the current architectural bottlenecks.
column45: Risks of not migrating are understood by senior leaders.
column46: There is clarity on how to evaluate ROI of platform investment.
column47: The business doesn’t over-index on vendor lock-in.
column48: Composable architecture has been validated through prototypes or PoCs.
column49: The leadership team reviews technical progress regularly.
column50: The platform roadmap is communicated transparently.
column51: Business leaders are open to rethinking operating models.
column52: There is a cross-functional steering group for the migration.
column53: Leadership encourages reuse of capabilities over duplication.
column54: Do we have clear, shared outcomes defined for the platform transformation?
column55: How confident are you in the business case and ROI behind the migration effort?
column56: Are business priorities and platform strategy reviewed together — or in isolation?
column57: Do you feel your peers across business and tech are aligned on why, when, and how to modernise?
column58: What trade-offs are you willing to make to ensure the platform evolves in the right direction?
column59: There is openness to change across the organisation.
column60: People are comfortable working in ambiguity.
column61: Teams have a growth mindset and seek continuous improvement.
column62: Failure is seen as a learning opportunity.
column64: Legacy systems are not emotionally defended.
column65: People understand the rationale for the migration.
column66: There are internal champions for change.
column67: Resistance is surfaced and discussed, not hidden.
column68: Celebrating wins is part of the change process.
column69: There is shared language around tech and product vision.
column70: The organisation has navigated change well in the past.
column71: People have opportunities to shape the future state.
column72: Product and engineering respect each other’s domain.
column74: There are mechanisms for feedback beyond surveys.
column75: People feel psychologically safe to speak up.
column76: Teams are proud of what they build.
column77: Leadership models the behaviour they ask for.
column78: People have time to learn and adapt.
column79: Change is communicated with empathy and clarity.
column80: There is organisational energy behind the migration.
column81: Innovation is encouraged even in core platforms.
column82: There’s transparency about trade-offs and priorities.
column83: There is enthusiasm about the future architecture.
column84: How are you preparing the organisation — not just the tech — for this migration?
column85: Do you feel leaders are modelling the behaviours they expect from others during change?
column86: Where are we strongest culturally — and where are we most vulnerable?
column87: How do you handle resistance to change when it comes from respected or senior individuals?
column88: Are incentives and KPIs aligned with the outcomes this transformation needs?
